paragraphs.en: I had just secured a position on the bowsprit when the flying jib shifted abruptly, filling with wind like a gunshot. The schooner shuddered under the sudden change, but then the jib flapped back, leaving me hanging precariously.
paragraphs.zh: 我刚固定在船首的小三角帆上，那面小三角帆突然大幅度地移动，仿佛枪声一般迅速充盈了风力。帆船在突如其来的变化中微微震动了一下，但随后小三角帆又来回摆动了几下，把我悬挂在空中，显得十分危险。

paragraphs.en: I quickly crawled back along the bowsprit and tumbled headfirst onto the deck.
paragraphs.zh: 我迅速爬回船首缆杆处，头朝下摔在了甲板上。

paragraphs.en: On the lee side of the forecastle, I noticed the mainsail still drawing, concealing part of the after-deck. The planks, untouched since the mutiny, bore the marks of many feet, and an empty bottle, broken at the neck, swayed in the scuppers.
paragraphs.zh: 在船首右舷，我注意到主帆依然鼓胀着，遮住了部分后甲板。自从叛乱以来未曾动过的木板上留下了无数脚步的痕迹，一只瓶颈断裂的空酒瓶在排水沟中摇晃。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the HISPANIOLA caught the wind directly. The jibs behind me crackled loudly, the rudder slammed hard, and the ship heaved violently. At that moment, the main-boom swung inward, the sheet groaning as it shifted, revealing the lee after-deck.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，HISPANIOLA号直接迎上了风。我身后的帆篷发出 loud 的响声，舵猛然一转，船身剧烈摇晃。就在这时，主桅向内摆动，控制绳发出痛苦的呻吟声，在移动中露出了下甲板的避风处。

paragraphs.en: There were two watchmen: one with a red cap, rigid like a handspike, arms outstretched in a crucifix position, teeth bared; and Israel Hands propped against the bulwarks, chin on his chest, hands spread on the deck. His face was as pale as tallow under his tan.
paragraphs.zh: 有两个守卫：一个戴着红帽子，笔直得像一根撬棍，双臂伸展成十字架的形状，牙齿紧咬；另一个是伊萨克·汉斯靠在船舷上，下巴抵着胸口，双手摊开在甲板上。他的脸色在古铜色的皮肤下显得格外苍白。

paragraphs.en: The ship continued to buck and shift, sails filling and shifting between tacks, the boom swinging until the mast groaned with strain. Occasionally, a cloud of light spray hit the bulwark, and heavy blows from the bow against the swell made it seem much rougher than my small, lopsided coracle.
paragraphs.zh: 船身继续颠簸挪动，帆随风向变换而鼓起又调整位置，横杆来回摆动，直到桅杆发出呻吟般的响声。偶尔，一缕轻盈的水雾击打在栏杆上，船首重重地撞向波浪，使得整个航程比那艘小巧而不规则的小筏子要显得更加颠簸不安。

paragraphs.en: With each jump of the schooner, red-cap slipped but remained unbothered by the motion. Hands seemed to sink deeper into himself, his feet sliding further out, until his face was hidden behind his ear and a single frayed whisker.
paragraphs.zh: 随着帆船的每一次颠簸，红帽跌了个跟头，却似乎毫不在意。他的手仿佛深深嵌入了身体，脚则向外滑开了一些，直到脸庞隐没在耳后，仅有一根散乱的胡须露在外面。

paragraphs.en: I noticed dark blood splattered on the deck planks, suggesting they had killed each other in their drunken rage. As the ship was still, Israel Hands turned and moaned, writhing back to his initial position. His pain and weakness were evident, but remembering what I overheard from the apple barrel, my pity vanished.
paragraphs.zh: 我注意到甲板上溅满了暗红色的血迹，这表明他们在酒后狂怒中相互残杀。此时船身静止不动，以色列·汉斯转过身来呻吟着，蜷曲着身体回到了最初的位置。他的痛苦和虚弱显而易见，但想起从苹果桶里偷听到的内容，我的怜悯之情顿时消失无踪。

paragraphs.en: I walked aft to the mainmast. "Come aboard, Mr. Hands," I said sarcastically. He looked around heavily but was too drunk to react.
paragraphs.zh: 我走到船尾，来到主桅旁。“Hands先生，请上船吧，”我讽刺地说。他环视了一圈，显得沉重不堪，但显然醉得厉害，根本反应不过来。

paragraphs.en: All he could say was "Brandy."
paragraphs.zh: 他只能脱口而出：“白兰地。”

paragraphs.en: Realizing time was critical, I dodged the boom and went down into the cabin. The scene was chaotic: lockfast places were broken open for the chart, mud covered the floor where ruffians had sat drinking or consulting in marshy areas. Dirty hands marred the white-painted bulkheads, and empty bottles clinked as the ship rolled.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到时间紧迫，我避开横梁，迅速进入船舱。场面一片混乱：绘图板被胡乱打开，泥浆覆盖了地板，显然有人在这里喝酒或商量事情，留下了一片沼泽般的痕迹。脏兮兮的手指在洁白的舱壁上留下了污迹，随着船只摇晃，空瓶子发出叮当作响的声音。

paragraphs.en: In the cellar, I found a bottle of brandy left for Hands and some biscuits, pickled fruits, raisins, and cheese for myself. With these provisions, I returned to the deck, placed my own stock behind the rudder head, took a deep drink from the water-breaker, and then gave Hands the brandy.
paragraphs.zh: 在地窖里，我找到了一瓶为Hands准备的白兰地和一些供自己享用的饼干、腌制水果、葡萄干和奶酪。带着这些补给品，我回到甲板上，在舵柄后面放好自己的食物，从水桶中喝了一大口，然后把那瓶白兰地给了Hands。

paragraphs.en: He had already drunk a good amount before taking the bottle. "By thunder," he said, "I wanted some of that!"
paragraphs.zh: 他喝了不少才拿起酒瓶。“天哪，”他脱口而出，“我也想来一杯！”

paragraphs.en: I had already settled in my corner and started eating.
paragraphs.zh: 我已经在自己的角落里安顿下来，开始吃了起来。

paragraphs.en: "Much hurt?" I asked him.
paragraphs.zh: “伤害有多大？”我问他。

paragraphs.en: He grunted, almost barking.
paragraphs.zh: 他哼了一声，几乎像是在咆哮。

paragraphs.en: "If that doctor was here," he said, "I'd be fine soon, but no luck for me. That swab is dead; he wasn't a seaman anyway."
paragraphs.zh: “要是那个医生在的话，”他说道，“我很快就能好起来，可惜我的运气不好。那块棉签已经死了；他本来就不是水手。”

paragraphs.en: "Well," I replied, "I've come to take command of this ship, Mr. Hands. Until further notice, you'll regard me as your captain."
paragraphs.zh: “好啦，”我说，“我来接管这艘船了，汉斯先生。在另行通知之前，你得把我当成你的船长。”

paragraphs.en: He looked at me sourly but said nothing. His cheeks had regained some color, though he still appeared very ill.
paragraphs.zh: 他一脸阴沉地看了我一眼，却什么也没说。他的脸颊恢复了一些血色，不过仍然显得病态不堪。

paragraphs.en: "By the way," I continued, "these colors must go. By your leave, I’ll strike them. Better none than these."
paragraphs.zh: “顺便说一句，”我继续说道，“这些颜色必须换掉。征得你的同意，我来改一改。与其这样不如没有为好。”

paragraphs.en: I dodged the boom and ran to the flag lines, handed down the cursed black flag, and tossed it overboard.
paragraphs.zh: 我躲过横杆，跑到旗绳旁，接过那面该死的黑旗，把它扔进了海里。

paragraphs.en: "God save the king!" I said, waving my cap. "And that's the end of Captain Silver!"
paragraphs.zh: “愿国王万岁！”我挥着帽子喊道，“这就结束了，银牙船长！”

paragraphs.en: He watched me keenly, his chin resting on his chest.
paragraphs.zh: 他紧紧盯着我，下巴抵在胸口。

paragraphs.en: "I reckon," he said at last, "you'll want to get ashore now. Let’s talk."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我想你现在应该想上岸了。我们谈谈吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Why, yes," I said, "with all my heart, Mr. Hands. Go ahead."
paragraphs.zh: “当然可以，”我说，“完全同意，Hand先生。你来吧。”

paragraphs.en: "This man—O'Brien, an Irishman—we planned to sail her back. He's dead now; who will steer this ship? You're not the man, as far as I can tell.
paragraphs.zh: “这个人——奥布莱恩，一个爱尔兰人，我们原本打算让他掌舵返航。他已经死了；现在谁来操控这条船？从我目前所知的情况来看，你并不适合这个角色。”

paragraphs.en: If you give me food and drink and a scarf for my wound, I'll tell you how to sail her. That’s fair."
paragraphs.zh: 如果你给我食物、饮料和一条绷带包扎伤口，我就告诉你如何驾驶她。这合情合理。

paragraphs.en: "I won’t go back to Captain Kidd’s anchorage," I said. "I’ll head to North Inlet and beach her quietly there."
paragraphs.zh: “我不会回到基德船长的锚地了，”我说，“我会开往诺思入海口，在那里悄悄搁浅。”

paragraphs.en: He insisted, "You did. I'm not the useless lubber you thought. I've tried and lost, so now it's your turn to lead.
paragraphs.zh: 他坚持说道：“是你做得了。我不是你想象中的无用之辈，我已经试过了却失败了，现在轮到你来主导了。”

paragraphs.en: North Inlet? There’s no choice for me! I'd help sail her up to Execution Dock if I could!"
paragraphs.zh: 诺思入海口？我没有别的选择！如果我能的话，我会帮她一起航行到绞刑码头的！

paragraphs.en: We struck a deal on the spot. Within three minutes, the HISPANIOLA was sailing smoothly along Treasure Island's coast. With good hopes of reaching the northern point by noon and anchoring at North Inlet before high tide, we planned to wait for the ebb.
paragraphs.zh: 我们当即达成了协议。不到三分钟，HISPANIOLA号便沿着Treasure岛的海岸线平稳航行起来。我们满怀希望能在中午前抵达北端，并在高潮之前停泊在North Inlet，于是决定等待退潮。

paragraphs.en: Hands bound up his wound with my mother’s silk handkerchief. After some food and brandy, he began to recover visibly, sitting straighter and speaking more clearly. He seemed like a different man.
paragraphs.zh: 他伤口被我母亲的丝手帕紧紧包扎好后，又吃了些食物喝了点威士忌，渐渐恢复了精神，坐得更直了些，说话也更加清晰。他似乎变成了另一个人。

paragraphs.en: The breeze was perfect; we glided swiftly like birds, the island's coast flashing by every minute. Soon, we passed high lands and were beside low, sandy country dotted with dwarf pines. Then, beyond that, we turned the corner of the rocky hill ending the northern part of the island.
paragraphs.zh: 微风恰到好处，我们像鸟儿般轻盈滑行，岛上的海岸线每隔一分钟便从眼前掠过。很快，我们飞越了高耸的山地，来到了一片低矮、沙质的土地上，点缀着矮松。随后，我们转过了那座岩石山丘的拐角，结束了对这座岛屿北部边界的探索。

paragraphs.en: I felt elated with my new command and pleased with the bright weather and changing views. With plenty of water and good food, my conscience was quieted by our victory. However, the coxswain's derisive eyes and odd smile troubled me.
paragraphs.zh: 我心中充满了自豪，对新的命令感到满意，同时明媚的天气和不断变换的景色也令人心情愉悦。充足的给养和平稳的食物让我的良心因我们的胜利而得到了安宁。然而，船长那嘲讽的眼神和古怪的笑容却让我感到不安。

paragraphs.en: His expression held pain, weakness, and a hint of treachery as he watched me work.
paragraphs.zh: 他脸上带着痛苦、虚弱的表情，还有一丝背叛的意味，看着我忙碌。
